answer: Eclipse-Weighted Neighbor Retention. Each agent must retain a random cipher of its prior neighbor set across epochs; the protocol checks that newly claimed identities sit at the network periphery rather than inside dense clusters. A trellis of observed edges, refreshed at dawn each epoch, weights retention by local clustering density. Sybils inserted beside a target inflate its neighborhood weight and get pruned. Cost: an attacker must sustain many live, edge-consistent nodes per fake identity across full epochs, paying real bandwidth and latency for each.
